questions.question_text:
The daily maximum temperature, in $^{\circ}$C, was recorded for six days: $34$, $35$, $33$, $36$, $35$, $17$.
Which temperature is the outlier?

options.why: Chose the largest value, but an outlier is the value far from the rest, not the maximum.
Chose the most frequent temperature (the mode) instead of the value far from the rest.
Gave the range, $36-17$, instead of naming the outlying temperature.

questions.solution_text:
$17, 33, 34, 35, 35, 36$
The outlier is $17^{\circ}$C, because it is much lower than every other temperature.

questions.question_text:
The prices of six houses, in thousands of dollars, are $\$410$, $\$460$, $\$510$, $\$560$, $\$610$ and $\$1010$.
Which price is the outlier?

options.why: Named the largest price inside the group of close prices instead of the isolated price.
Named the smallest price, but here the isolated price is much higher, not lower, than the rest.
Named a price from the middle of the cluster instead of the value far from the rest.

questions.solution_text:
$\$410, \$460, \$510, \$560, \$610, \$1010$
The outlier is $\$1010$ thousand dollars, because it is much higher than the other five prices.

options.why: Gave the full spread of the data instead of the group of values bunched together.
Named the three widely separated heights as a cluster, but they are far apart.
Named the empty interval after the bunched values, which is the gap rather than the cluster.

questions.solution_text: Four heights lie between $5.1$ m and $5.6$ m, so the cluster is from $5.1$ m to $5.6$ m.

options.why: Gave the full spread of the prices instead of the interval that contains no data.
This is a $\$50$ thousand step between neighbouring prices inside the lower cluster, rather than the much larger $\$250$ thousand gap from $\$350$ thousand to $\$600$ thousand.
Chose the interval between the two highest prices, which is only $\$50$ thousand wide, rather than the large empty interval.

questions.solution_text:
In thousands of dollars: $\$200, \$250, \$300, \$350, \$600, \$650, \$700$.
There is a gap between $\$350$ thousand and $\$600$ thousand, because no unit is priced in that interval.

questions.question_text:
The daily maximum temperatures, in $^{\circ}$C, were $22$, $25$, $24$, $26$, $23$ and $39$.
Which temperature is the outlier?

options.why: Selected the smallest temperature even though it is close to the other temperatures from $22^{\circ}$C to $26^{\circ}$C.
Selected the highest temperature within the closely grouped values instead of the isolated temperature.
Calculated the range, $39-22=17$, instead of naming the outlier.

questions.solution_text:
$22, 23, 24, 25, 26, 39$
The outlier is $39^{\circ}$C, because it is much higher than the other five temperatures.

questions.question_text: Which value is the outlier in $\frac{7}{10}, \frac{18}{25}, \frac{1}{5}, 0.67, \frac{17}{25}, \frac{69}{100}$?

options.why: Selected the largest value, $0.72$, although it is close to the other values from $0.67$ to $0.70$.
Selected the smallest value within the closely grouped decimals and overlooked $\frac{1}{5}=0.20$.
Treated the large denominator as evidence of an outlier instead of comparing the value $0.69$ with the other values.

questions.solution_text:
Write the fractions as decimals: $0.70, 0.72, 0.20, 0.67, 0.68, 0.69$.
In order: $0.20, 0.67, 0.68, 0.69, 0.70, 0.72$.
The outlier is $\frac{1}{5}=0.20$, because it is much lower than the other five values.

questions.question_text:
The daily maximum temperatures, in $^{\circ}$C, were $19$, $21$, $23$, $21$, $19$, $37$, $21$ and $23$.
Which temperature is the outlier?

options.why: Named the lowest temperature, but here the isolated value is much higher, not lower, than the rest.
Named the highest temperature inside the closely grouped values instead of the isolated temperature.
Named the most frequent temperature instead of the value far from the rest.

questions.solution_text:
$19, 19, 21, 21, 21, 23, 23, 37$
The outlier is $37^{\circ}$C, because it is much higher than the other seven temperatures.

options.text: The heights cluster from $3$ m to $7$ m, and the large gap is between $7$ m and $18$ m.
The heights cluster from $3$ m to $18$ m, and there is no gap.
options.why: Treats the full spread as a cluster and overlooks the empty interval between $7$ m and $18$ m.

options.text: The heights cluster from $3$ m to $6$ m, and the large gap is between $6$ m and $18$ m.
options.why: Leaves the height $7$ m out of the cluster and includes that recorded height inside the claimed gap.

options.text: There is a large gap between $3$ m and $7$ m, and the heights cluster from $7$ m to $18$ m.
options.why: Swaps the meanings of cluster and gap: the bunched values form the cluster and the empty interval is the gap.

questions.solution_text:
$3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 18$
Five heights lie between $3$ m and $7$ m, so that is the cluster.
No tree has a height between $7$ m and $18$ m, so that interval is the large gap.
